subneolithic.name: Subneolithic
subneolithic.summary: An archaeological period for cultures transitional between the Mesolithic and Neolithic, which adopted pottery but kept economies based on hunting, gathering and fishing.

erteb-lle-culture.name: Ertebølle culture
erteb-lle-culture.summary: A hunter-gatherer, pottery-making culture of southern Scandinavia (c. 5400–3950 BCE), named for shell-midden sites found in Danish Jutland.

funnelbeaker-culture.name: Funnelbeaker culture
funnelbeaker-culture.summary: A Neolithic archaeological culture in north-central Europe, about 4100 to 2800 BCE, that brought farming and husbandry to pottery-using hunter-gatherers north of the Elbe and Vistula rivers.

iijoki.name: Iijoki River
iijoki.summary: A 370-kilometre river in Finland's North Ostrobothnia region, flowing into the Gulf of Bothnia with many tributaries and about 150 rapids.

maglemosian-culture.name: Maglemosian culture
maglemosian-culture.summary: An early Mesolithic culture of Northern Europe, roughly 9000 to 6000 BCE, later succeeded in Scandinavia by the Kongemose culture.

kongemose-culture.name: Kongemose culture
kongemose-culture.summary: A Mesolithic hunter-gatherer culture in southern Scandinavia from about 6000 to 5200 BC, known for long flint blades shaped into rhombic arrowheads.

pitted-ware-culture.name: Pitted Ware culture
pitted-ware-culture.summary: A hunter-gatherer culture of coastal southern Scandinavia (c. 3500–2300 BC), known for maritime hunting and trade with farming communities before being absorbed into the Battle Axe culture.

battle-axe-culture.name: Battle Axe culture
battle-axe-culture.summary: A Chalcolithic culture of southern Scandinavia and southwest Finland, about 2800 to 2300 BCE, thought to have spread Indo-European languages to the region and to have evolved into the Nordic Bronze Age.

norrland.name: Norrland
norrland.summary: The northernmost and largest of Sweden's three traditional lands, covering about 60% of the country's area but only about 12% of its population.

doggerland.name: Doggerland
doggerland.summary: A now-submerged area of land in Northern Europe that once connected Britain to the mainland, flooded by rising seas between about 10,000 and 7,000 years ago.

dalsland.name: Dalsland
dalsland.summary: A sparsely populated Swedish province west of Lake Vänern, nicknamed 'Sweden's lake province' for its dense forests and many lakes.

v-sterg-tland.name: Västergötland
v-sterg-tland.summary: One of Sweden's traditional provinces, in the southwest of the country, home to the city of Gothenburg.

sterg-tland.name: Östergötland
sterg-tland.summary: A traditional province in southern Sweden bordering the Baltic Sea, also known in English as East Gothland.

svealand.name: Svealand
svealand.summary: The historical core region of south-central Sweden, one of its three historical lands, home to the Svear people from whom the name "Swedes" derives.

fennoscandia.name: Fennoscandia
fennoscandia.summary: Peninsula in northern Europe encompassing the Scandinavian and Kola peninsulas, mainland Finland, and Karelia.

ancient-north-eurasian.name: Ancient North Eurasian
ancient-north-eurasian.summary: An ancestral genetic lineage tracing to the Mal'ta–Buret' culture in Siberia around 24,000 years ago, formed from a mix of ancient West and East Eurasian peoples.

n-stvet-and-lihult-cultures.name: Nøstvet and Lihult cultures
n-stvet-and-lihult-cultures.summary: Two closely related Mesolithic hunter-gatherer traditions in Scandinavia, around the Oslofjord and western Sweden, lasting from about 6200 to 3200 BCE before giving way to farming cultures.

alvastra-pile-dwelling.name: Alvastra pile-dwelling
alvastra-pile-dwelling.summary: A stilt dwelling from around 3000 BC in Sweden, unique in Northern Europe, that served as a tribe's seasonal religious centre where Funnelbeaker and Pitted Ware culture objects were both found.

kunda-culture.name: Kunda culture
kunda-culture.summary: Mesolithic hunter-gatherer culture of the Baltic forest zone dating to about 8500–5000 BC, named after the Estonian town of Kunda, later succeeded by the Narva culture.

haplogroup-r1a.name: Haplogroup R1a1a1
haplogroup-r1a.summary: A Y-chromosome lineage spanning Scandinavia to Central Asia and South Asia, whose main subclade diversified roughly 3,400 to 5,800 years ago and is central to debates on Indo-European origins.

haplogroup-n-m231.name: Haplogroup N-M231
haplogroup-n-m231.summary: A Y-chromosome lineage most common among men from northern Eurasia, with its rarest form found only in China and Cambodia, suggesting an East or Southeast Asian origin.

ancylus-lake.name: Ancylus age
ancylus-lake.summary: The era of Ancylus Lake, a large freshwater lake in northern Europe from about 8,750 to 7,850 BC and one of the predecessors of the modern Baltic Sea.

littorina-sea.name: Littorina Sea
littorina-sea.summary: A brackish-water stage of the Baltic Sea that existed around 8500 to 4000 BP, following the Ancylus Lake, named after the periwinkle mollusc common in its waters.

herc2.name: HERC2
herc2.summary: A gene encoding a giant enzyme involved in DNA repair, pigmentation and neurological disorders; certain versions of it are linked to eye and skin colour.

membrane-associated-transporter-protein.name: SLC45A2
membrane-associated-transporter-protein.summary: A human gene encoding a membrane protein linked to skin pigmentation, also called the melanoma antigen AIM1.

sodium-potassium-calcium-exchanger-5.name: SLC24A5
sodium-potassium-calcium-exchanger-5.summary: A gene that strongly influences human skin colour; a variant linked to lighter skin in Europeans is thought to have spread through selection over thousands of years.

eastern-hunter-gatherer.name: Eastern hunter-gatherers
eastern-hunter-gatherer.summary: A genetic ancestry group representing the Mesolithic hunter-gatherers of Eastern Europe, derived mainly from Ancient North Eurasian ancestry that came from Siberia.

trelleborgs-museum.name: Trelleborgs Museum
trelleborgs-museum.summary: A local history museum in Trelleborg, southern Sweden, notable for a reconstruction of a Viking longhouse and of a hunter-gatherer from about 7,000 years ago found nearby.

dal-lven.name: Dalälven
dal-lven.summary: A river in central Sweden, one of its longest, historically used to transport timber by raft and commonly seen as marking the southern border of Norrland.

comb-ceramic-culture.name: Comb Ceramic culture
comb-ceramic-culture.summary: A northeast European culture, roughly 4200 to 2000 BCE, marked by pit-comb pottery and a mostly hunter-gatherer lifestyle with some early farming.

saimaa.name: Saimaa
saimaa.summary: The largest lake in Finland and the fourth-largest natural freshwater lake in Europe, covering about 4,279 square kilometres in southeastern Finland's Lakeland region.

lake-onega.name: Lake Onega
lake-onega.summary: The second-largest lake in Europe, in northwestern Russia, dotted with about 1,650 islands including Kizhi, known for its historic wooden churches.

valdai-hills.name: Valdai Hills
valdai-hills.summary: An upland region in north-west central European Russia between Saint Petersburg and Moscow, popular for fishing and home to a national park since 1990.

swiderian-culture.name: Swiderian culture
swiderian-culture.summary: An Upper Palaeolithic and Mesolithic culture centred on modern Poland, developed on sand dunes left behind by retreating glaciers.

r-gen.name: Rügen
r-gen.summary: Germany's largest island, in the Baltic Sea off the Pomeranian coast, known for sandy beaches, chalk cliffs, and its Jasmund National Park.

komsa-culture.name: Komsa culture
komsa-culture.summary: A Mesolithic hunter-gatherer culture in northern Norway from around 10,000 BC, named after Mount Komsa where its remains were first found in 1925.

varangerfjord.name: Varangerfjord
varangerfjord.summary: Norway's easternmost fjord, in Finnmark county near the Russian border, associated with early prehistoric coastal settlement in the region.

narva-culture.name: Narva culture
narva-culture.summary: A Neolithic hunter-gatherer culture of the eastern Baltic region, spanning about 5300 to 1750 BC and named after Estonia's Narva River.

flintbek.name: Flintbek
flintbek.summary: A municipality in Schleswig-Holstein, Germany, where cart tracks from about 3400 BCE were found under a megalithic long barrow, the earliest known direct evidence of wheeled vehicles anywhere.
